full_name_ar: أنيس بن الضحاك ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists Unays ibn al-Dahhak al-Aslami, noting that Abu Hatim al-Razi said he is not known. Ibn Mandah narrated from him, via Amr ibn Muslim, a hadith in which the Prophet told Abu Dharr to wear coarse clothing; Ibn Mandah called it gharib and mursal. Ibn Hibban and Ibn Abd al-Barr held he is the Unays told 'go, O Unays, to this man's wife', but Ibn Hajar doubts this and thinks he is someone else.

full_name_ar: الأسود بن أصرم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba quotes Ibn Hibban that he is counted among the people of al-Sham, and Abu Zur'a al-Dimashqi, Ibn Sumay' and Ibn Abd al-Barr list him among companions who settled in al-Sham. Al-Baghawi said he knew no other hadith from him, and al-Bukhari said its chain needs examination.

Abu Bakr ibn Isa in Tarikh al-Himsiyyin lists him among companions who settled in Homs, as distinct from Shurahbil ibn Aws, while al-Baghawi held the correct name is Shurahbil ibn Aws. Via Nimran he narrated the hadith that whoever walks with a wrongdoer to help him, knowing he is a wrongdoer, has left faith.

It quotes al-Baladhuri that he was Abyssinian with the kunya Abu Mariya. The entry cites the hadith, reported by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and both Sahihs via Anas, in which the Prophet told him: 'Gently, Anjasha, with the glass vessels (the women).'

Al-Barudi and Ibn Mandah report, via Rafi' ibn Khadij, that a man of Banu Sulaym called Isaf ibn Anmar mocked the Ansar in verse over the ban on renting farmland, and their poet Isaf ibn Nahik answered him; Ibn Mandah called it gharib. Ibn Hajar remarks that nothing in the report proves he was a companion.

full_name_ar: أميمة مولاة رسول ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists Umayma, freedwoman of the Messenger of God, and quotes Abu Umar (Ibn Abd al-Barr) that she served the Prophet and that her hadith is with the people of al-Sham. Her report, transmitted via Jubayr ibn Nufayr, describes her pouring ablution water for the Prophet when a man asked for advice, and he replied: 'Do not associate anything with God, even if you are cut or burned.' Ibn al-Sakan notes a similar mursal version attributed to Umm Ayman.

full_name_ar: بشر بن معاوية ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba gives his lineage as Bishr ibn Mu'awiya ibn Thawr of Banu al-Bakka' of Amir ibn Sa'sa'a. It quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a companion counted among the people of the Hijaz, who came as a delegate with his father. Al-Bukhari and al-Baghawi report that he came with his father Mu'awiya ibn Thawr to the Prophet, who wiped his head and prayed for him, leaving a mark like a blaze on his face; al-Baghawi called the narrator Imran unknown.

full_name_ar: بشر بن عقربة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists Bishr ibn Uqraba al-Juhani, kunya Abu al-Yaman, saying he and his father were companions; some call him Bashir, but al-Bukhari held Bishr more correct. Via Abd Allah ibn Awf he related that his father was martyred with the Prophet, and the Prophet comforted him as he wept, saying: 'Are you not pleased that I be your father and A'isha your mother?' Al-Bukhari noted that Bishr is known in Palestine.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3093, Sabra bin al-Fakih) says he is also called Ibn al-Fakiha or Ibn Abi al-Fakih al-Makhzumi, or al-Asadi, a companion who settled in Kufa. He has one hadith in al-Nasa'i with a good (hasan) chain about Satan lying in wait for the son of Adam, which Ibn Hibban graded authentic. 'Umara bin Khuzayma and Salim bin Abi al-Ja'd narrated from him.

full_name_ar: سويد بن زيد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3611) says he was the brother of Rifa'a, listed by Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli among companions who settled in Palestine; Ibn Hibban said he had companionship and died at Bayt Jibrin. Ibn Manda says he came in a delegation with his brothers to the Prophet. Ibn Hisham, al-Umawi, al-Waqidi and al-Tabari report he was among the Banu Judham captured when Zayd bin Haritha raided them; they accepted Islam and the Prophet released them.

full_name_ar: سويد بن قيس أبو مرحب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3620) lists Suwayd bin Qays al-'Abdi, Abu Marhab. Simak bin Harb narrated from him that the Prophet bought a pair of trousers (sarawil) from him, a report in Ahmad and the Sunan collections, with disagreement over Simak's chain. Ibn Hajar notes al-Mizzi's wording wrongly implies Suwayd's kunya was Abu Safwan.

full_name_ar: سويد الجهني والد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3631) lists Suwayd al-Juhani, or al-Muzani, also called al-Ansari, father of 'Uqba; Ibn Hibban said he had companionship. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) says his hadiths, on lost property and on Mount Uhud ('it loves us and we love it'), are with al-Zuhri and Rabi'a via his son and are sound. Al-Zuhri reports from 'Uqba bin Suwayd that his father said the Prophet, returning from Khaybar, saw Uhud and said this.

The report is unnamed in al-Bukhari, and named in Ahmad, al-Daraqutni, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya'la, Muslim, Abu Dawud and Ibn Khuzayma via Jabir and Abu Hurayra.

Ibn Abi Khaythama and al-Ruyani in his Musnad report via Abu Ja'far al-Baqir that he came in to 'Umar, who addressed him.

full_name_ar: سباع بن عرفطة ( رضي الله عنه

Abu Hurayra reports arriving in Medina while the Prophet was at Khaybar, having appointed Siba' bin 'Urfuta as his deputy over Medina; they prayed the dawn prayer behind him.

Through a chain via Baqiyya, Dubara bin Malik al-Hadrami and 'Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr from his father, he narrated from the Prophet: 'It is great treachery to tell your brother something he believes from you while you are lying to him.'

full_name_ar: سفيان بن وهب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3343) lists Sufyan bin Wahb al-Khawlani, Abu Ayman; Abu Hatim said he had companionship. Ibn Yunus said he came to the Prophet, witnessed the conquest of Egypt, governed Ifriqiya under 'Abd al-'Aziz bin Marwan, and died in 82 AH. He narrated the hadith 'the hundred [years] will not come while anyone [of those alive now] remains on the earth'. Ibn Hibban wavered, listing him both among companions (settled in Egypt) and among the Successors.

bio: Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab (entry 3386) lists Samra' bint Nahik al-Asadiyya, who met the Messenger of God and lived long. She used to walk through the markets enjoining good and forbidding evil, striking people for it with a whip she carried.

He narrated that he fell ill after coming to the Prophet and wished to drink from the water of the Batha', but his hijra held him back; the Prophet told him 'Go, you are an emigrant wherever you are.' Ibn Abi Hatim says his grandson Qayzi bin 'Amr bin Shaddad narrated from him.

In it the Prophet said of the wine-drinker 'Flog him', and on the fourth occasion 'Kill him'.

Ibn al-Sakan counted him among the Kufans and said he narrated only one hadith from the Prophet. Ahmad transmits from Nubayt bin Shurayt that he rode behind his father at the Farewell Pilgrimage and heard the Prophet say 'Your blood and your property are sacred to you'.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4315) gives his name as Tahfa, also spelled Takhfa or Tughfa, and says al-Bukhari preferred Takhfa in his al-Tarikh al-Awsat. He was one of the Ahl al-Suffa, and his hadith forbidding sleeping on the belly is found in Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and others. His son Ya'ish ibn Takhfa ibn Qays transmitted from him, and some reports attribute the narration to his son 'Abdullah ibn Tahfa instead.

It reports Ibn Hibban saying he was eight years old when the Prophet died, and al-Tabari saying he accepted Islam together with his father. It notes that al-Bukhari and Ibn Hibban placed him among the Successors (Tabi'un) even though some reports have him narrating from the Prophet.

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن عبد نهم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4822) identifies him as al-Muzani, known as Dhu al-Bijadayn, a name reportedly given by the Prophet after his uncle stripped him of his possessions when he became Muslim. It describes him as constant in loud dhikr and Qur'an recitation, and reports 'Umar calling him one of the awwahin. He died during the Tabuk expedition, and Ibn Mas'ud's account says the Prophet himself saw to his burial and prayed for him; sources cited include Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Manda and Ahmad.

Ibn Abi Khaythama and Ibn al-Sakan affirmed his companionship, while Abu Hatim said he did not know him. His hadith is recorded by Abu Dawud and was also reported through another chain.

full_name_ar: عمرو بن عبد الله البكالي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6004, 'Amr al-Bikali) says his father's name is disputed: Sufyan, Sayf or 'Abdullah. It quotes al-Bukhari that he was a companion, notes Khalifa and Ibn al-Barqi listed him among the companions, and says he was the brother of Nawf al-Bikali and lived in Syria, with a house in Homs. It also reports he came to Egypt with Marwan ibn al-Hakam in the year 65.
research_evidence: عمرو البكالي بكسر الموحدة وتخفيف الكاف. اختلف في اسم أبيه، فقيل سفيان، وقيل سيف، وقيل عبد اللَّه.

full: 'Amr bin M'adi Karb bin 'Abdullah bin 'Amr bin 'Asim bin 'Amr bin Zubayd
full_name_ar: عمرو بن معدي كرب بن عبد الله ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5984) gives his lineage back to Zubayd and calls him al-Zubaydi, the famous poet and horseman, with the kunya Abu Thawr. It states he had companionship and narration, and that he fought well at the Battle of al-Qadisiyya. The editor's footnote points to Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isti'ab, al-Muhabbar and Ibn Hisham's Sira.
research_evidence: ٥٩٨٤- عمرو بن معديكرب بن عبد اللَّه بن عمرو بن عصم بن زبيد الأصغر بن ربيعة بن سلمة بن مازن بن ربيعة بن منبه

full_name_ar: عقبة مولى جبر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5637, 'Uqba al-Farisi) describes him as the client (mawla) of Jabr ibn 'Atik al-Ansari. It says Khalifa listed him among the companions who were clients of Banu Hashim, but called him Abu 'Uqba.
research_evidence: ٥٦٣٧ ز- عقبة الفارسيّ: مولى جبر بن عتيك الأنصاري. ذكره خليفة في موالي بني هاشم من الصحابة، لكن قال أبو عقبة.

full_name_ar: عبيد بن عمرو الكلابي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5367) quotes al-Bukhari that 'Ubayd ibn 'Amr al-Kilabi was a companion, noting that Abu Ma'mar al-Ghutayfi called him 'Ubayda. It cites a report via Sa'id ibn Khuthaym from his grandmother Rab'iya that her grandfather 'Ubayda ibn 'Amr al-Kilabi saw the Prophet perform ablution thoroughly.
research_evidence: عبيد بن عمرو الكلابي قال البخاريّ: له صحبة، قال: وقال أبو معمر الغطيفي عبيدة بن عمرو- يعني بزيادة هاء

full_name_ar: عبيد بن قيس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5371) describes 'Ubayd ibn Qays as al-Ansari al-Mazini, well known by his kunya. It notes that Ibn 'Abd al-Barr wrote the name as 'Ubayd ibn Qushayr, and that Ibn Hibban gave his name as Nashib while al-Mizzi gave it as Harb. (The kunya on this page could not be read reliably, so it is not recorded here.)
research_evidence: ٥٣٧١- عبيد بن قيس | الأنصاري المازني . مشهور بكنيته. ووقع عند ابن عبد البر عبيد بن قشير

full_name_ar: عويمر بن الحارث ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6129) identifies 'Uwaymir as the son of Abu Abyad al-'Ajlani, and quotes al-Tabarani that he is 'Uwaymir ibn al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Jabir, 'Abyad' being a nickname of one of his ancestors. A separate short entry (6133, 'Uwaymir ibn al-Harith) cross-refers to this one. The entry cites reports about him from al-Bukhari and Muslim and from al-Muwatta'.
research_evidence: هو ابن أبي أبيض العجلاني. وقال الطبراني: هو عويمر بن الحارث بن زيد بن جابر

full_name_ar: العلاء بن سبع ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5661) quotes Ibn Hibban that al-'Ala' ibn Sab' was a companion. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) reported a view that he is al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami, but Ibn Hajar doubts this because al-Bukhari treated them as two different people.
research_evidence: ٥٦٦١- العلاء بن سبع: قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة. وقال أبو عمر: قيل إنه هو العلاء بن الحضرميّ.

full_name_ar: عمارة بن أوس له ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Abi Hatim's al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (entry 2001) states that 'Umara ibn Aws was a companion. It says Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqa narrated from him, in the transmission of Qays ibn al-Rabi'.

full_name_ar: عمارة بن عبيد شيخ ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5738) quotes Ibn Hibban calling him 'a very old shaykh' and saying Dawud ibn Abi Hind claimed he was a companion. Dawud ibn Abi Hind transmitted from him a hadith about five trials to befall the community, found in Ahmad's collection. The entry notes disagreement over whether his name was 'Umara or 'Ammar and whether he was a companion or a successor.
research_evidence: ٥٧٣٨- عمارة بن عبيد الخثعميّ: ويقال ابن عبيد اللَّه. ويقال عمار. قال ابن حبّان: شيخ كبير، كان داود بن أبي هند يزعم أنّ له صحبة.

full_name_ar: عمارة بن عامر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5736) names him 'Umara ibn 'Amir ibn al-Mushannaj al-Qushayri. It says Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Ghallabi, in his history, reported from a man of Banu 'Amir from Syria that Mu'awiya and 'Umara ibn al-Mushannaj of Banu Qushayr were companions of the Prophet. Al-Khatib cited him in al-Mu'talif via al-Ghallabi.
research_evidence: ٥٧٣٦- عمارة بن عامر: بن المشنّج، بمعجمة ونون مشددة بعدها جيم، القشيري.

full_name_ar: عتبة بن عبد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5423) gives his kunya as Abu al-Walid and says the Prophet renamed him 'Utba (his earlier name is given as 'Utla or Nushba). He was present at the siege of Qurayza and narrated about it. His son Yahya ibn 'Utba and Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd transmitted from him; the entry gives differing death dates and says he lived to 94.
research_evidence: عتبة بن عبد: بغير إضافة. قال البخاري: ويقال ابن عبد اللَّه. ولا يصح.

full_name_ar: عتبة بن أسيد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5413) identifies him as Abu Basir al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra, well known by his kunya. After the Treaty of al-Hudaybiya he escaped Mecca, and others joined him on the coast, where they raided Quraysh caravans. The entry says he died holding a letter from the Prophet calling him to Medina, and Abu Jandal buried him.
research_evidence: ٥٤١٣- عتبة بن أسيد: بالفتح، ابن جارية، بالجيم، ابن أسيد بالفتح أيضا، ابن عبد اللَّه بن غيرة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عتبة بن سالم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5417) lists him as 'Utba bin Salim bin Harmala al-'Adawi and states he was a Companion. It notes that al-Mustaghfiri mentioned him and added nothing more.
research_evidence: عتبة بن سالم بن حرملة العدوي. له صحبة. ذكره المستغفري، ولم يزد.

full_name_ar: عتبة بن يزيد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5433) lists 'Utba bin Yazid al-Sulami. It quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a Companion, and notes Ibn Hibban treated him as distinct from 'Utba bin al-Nuddar al-Sulami, while Ibn Hajar suspects they are the same person.
research_evidence: عتبة بن يزيد السلمي. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة، وفرق بينه وبين عتبة بن الندّر السلمي.

full_name_ar: عمير بن فروة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6085) lists 'Umayra bin Farwa al-Kindi, father of al-'Urs and 'Adi, sons of 'Umayra. full_name_ar: عمير بن جابر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6038) lists 'Umayr bin Jabir bin Ghadira bin Ashras al-Kindi as a Companion. The entry cites Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, Ibn al-Sakan, Ibn Abi Khaythama and al-Baghawi. No death year is given.
research_evidence: عمير بن جابر بن غاضرة بن أشرس الكندي

full_name_ar: عمير بن عمرو بن عمير ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6061) lists 'Umayr bin 'Amr bin 'Umayr al-Ansari. It states that Ibn Hibban mentioned him in the first generation (tabaqa) and said he was a Companion.
research_evidence: عمير بن عمرو بن عمير الأنصاري. ذكره ابن حبان في الطبقة الأولى، وقال: له صحبة.

full_name_ar: عبادة بن قرص ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4519) lists him as 'Ubada bin Qurt or Qurs, of the tribe of Layth bin Bakr of Kinana, who settled in Basra. It cites Ibn Hibban for his companionship and for his death in the year 41, when the Kharijites seized and killed him near al-Ahwaz. His narrations were recorded by Ahmad (via Humayd bin Hilal), al-Tayalisi, al-Tabarani and al-Baghawi.
research_evidence: عبادة بن قرط: أو قرص بن عروة بن بجير بن مالك بن قيس بن عامر بن ليث بن بكر بن عبد مناة بن كنانة

full_name_ar: عتاب بن شمير ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5410) lists 'Attab bin Shumayr (also given as Numayr) al-Dabbi and quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a Companion. It cites al-Baghawi that he settled in Kufa, and relates a hadith in which he asked the Prophet's permission to visit his elderly father and siblings to invite them to Islam.
research_evidence: عتاب بن شمير: بالمعجمة. وقيل نمير، بالنون، الضبي. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد بن زمعة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5289) lists 'Abd bin Zam'a al-Qurashi al-'Amiri, brother of Sawda, Mother of the Believers, and says he became Muslim on the day Mecca was conquered. It cites the two Sahih collections for his dispute with Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas over the son of Zam'a's slave-woman, which the Prophet decided in his favour. It quotes Ibn 'Abd al-Barr describing him as one of the prominent Companions.
research_evidence: عبد بن زمعة بن قيس بن عبد شمس بن عبد ودّ بن نصر بن مالك بن حسل بن عامر بن لؤيّ القرشي العامري، أخو سودة أم المؤمنين.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عباد بن عبد عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba has a cross-reference entry 'Abbad bin 'Abd 'Amr (entry 4488) pointing to the main entry 'Iyadh bin 'Amr or bin 'Abd 'Amr al-Azdi or al-Sulami (entry 6136), noting the name is also read 'Abbad. It says he is mentioned as a Companion by al-Hasan bin Sufyan and al-Tabarani, and that reports describe him serving the Prophet.
research_evidence: عياذ بفتح أوله وتشديد ثانيه وآخره معجمة، ابن عمرو، أو ابن عبد عمرو، الأزدي أو السلمي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عيينة بن حصن ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6166, beginning on page 2381) lists 'Uyayna bin Hisn bin Hudhayfa bin Badr al-Fazari, Abu Malik, as a Companion who was among those whose hearts were reconciled (al-mu'allafa), with no authentic narration from him. It says he became Muslim before the conquest of Mecca, took part in Hunayn and al-Ta'if, and was sent by the Prophet against Banu Tamim. It adds that he apostatized under Abu Bakr and supported Tulayha before returning to Islam, and records the epithet 'the obeyed fool' (al-ahmaq al-muta').
research_evidence: ابن لوذان بن ثعلبة بن عدي فزارة الفزاري، أبو مالك ... له صحبة. وكان من المؤلفة، ولم يصح له رواية

full_name_ar: عروة بن مالك الأسلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5538) lists 'Urwa bin Malik al-Aslami and quotes Ibn Hibban, followed by al-Mustaghfiri and Abu Musa, that he was a Companion. It cites Ibn Sa'd and al-Bawardi that he fought at Siffin with 'Ali, and notes 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Rafi' also listed him among the Companions present at Siffin.
research_evidence: عروة بن مالك الأسلمي قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة، وتبعه المستغفريّ. وأورده أبو موسى بذلك، ولم يورد له شيئا.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: علقمة بن الفغواء ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5692) lists 'Alqama bin al-Faghwa' bin 'Ubayd bin 'Amr bin Mazin al-Khuza'i and quotes Ibn Hibban and Ibn al-Kalbi that he was a Companion. It relates, via Ibn Ishaq and others, that the Prophet sent him with money to Abu Sufyan bin Harb for the poor of Quraysh, telling him to take 'Amr bin Umayya as a travelling companion.

full_name_ar: علقمة بن الحويرث ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5682, heading on page 2195) lists 'Alqama bin al-Huwayrith al-Ghifari and quotes Ibn Hibban that he is said to have been a Companion. It cites Khalifa (bin Khayyat) for a report through Muhammad bin Mutarrif's grandmother, who heard it from 'Alqama, and notes al-Bukhari, al-Tabarani, Ibn Manda and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr recorded this narration.
research_evidence: قال ابن حبّان: يقال: إن له صحبة. وقال خليفة: حدثنا محمد بن مطرف، حدثتني جدتي، سمعت علقمة بن الحويرث الغفاريّ

full_name_ar: علقمة بن رمثة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5685) lists 'Alqama bin Rimtha al-Balawi and quotes Abu Hatim that he was a Companion. It cites Ibn Yunus that he gave the pledge under the tree and witnessed the conquest of Egypt. His report about the Prophet sending 'Amr bin al-'As to Bahrain was transmitted via Zuhayr bin Qays al-Balawi and recorded by al-Bukhari, Ibn Yunus, Ahmad, al-Baghawi and Ibn Manda.
research_evidence: علقمة بن رمثة: بكسر أوله وسكون الميم بعدها مثلثة، البلوي. قال أبو حاتم: له صحبة. وقال ابن يونس: بايع تحت الشجرة، وشهد فتح مصر.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: علقمة بن علاثة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5691) lists 'Alqama bin 'Ulatha, of the Ja'far bin Kilab branch of Banu 'Amir bin Sa'sa'a. It notes he appears in the Sahih collections in a report from Abu Sa'id that the Prophet distributed gold among four men, including 'Alqama bin 'Ulatha, 'Uyayna bin Hisn and al-Aqra' bin Habis.
research_evidence: علقمة بن علاثة: بن عوف بن الأحوص بن جعفر بن كلاب بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صعصعة العامري.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عدي بن بداء ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5489) says 'Adi bin Badda' is mentioned in the story of Tamim al-Dari connected to the revelation of Qur'an 5:106, where both are described as Christians who travelled for trade. The entry notes that Ibn Hibban counted him a Companion and Ibn Manda included him, while Abu Nu'aym and others disputed his companionship.
research_evidence: عدي بن بدّاء: بتشديد الدال قبلها موحدة مفتوحة. له ذكر في قصة تميم الدّاريّ

full_name_ar: عرفة بن ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6923) lists him as Ghurfa bin al-Harith al-Kindi, Abu al-Harith al-Yamani, who settled in Egypt, and notes that Abu Nu'aym gave the name as 'Arafa al-Kindi. It quotes Abu Hatim and Ibn al-Sakan that he was a Companion, and reports that he fought the apostates in Yemen alongside 'Ikrima bin Abi Jahl.

full_name_ar: عرفجة بن أبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5526) lists 'Arfaja bin Abi Yazid and quotes Ibn Hibban that he is said to have been a Companion. It also quotes Abu Musa that Ja'far (al-Mustaghfiri) listed him among the Companions without citing any report from him.
research_evidence: عرفجة بن أبي يزيد: قال ابن حبّان: يقال إن له صحبة. وقال أبو موسى: ذكره جعفر في الصحابة ولم يورد له شيئا

It notes Ibn Manda gave the name with sin instead of tha', and that al-Tabarani recorded a hadith from him: 'We have more right to doubt than Ibrahim.'

full_name_ar: عنبسة بن ربيعة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6090) lists 'Anbasa bin Rabi'a al-Juhani and quotes Ibn Hibban that he is said to have been a Companion. It notes Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri followed Ibn Hibban and Abu Musa added him in his supplement.
research_evidence: عنبسة بن ربيعة الجهنيّ: قال ابن حبّان: يقال له صحبة، وتبعه جعفر المستغفري. واستدركه أبو موسى.

full_name_ar: عرزب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5518) lists 'Urzub al-Kindi, counted among the people of al-Sham, and says al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Sakan and others mentioned him; Ibn Hibban expressed doubt about his companionship. Ibn Manda transmitted a single hadith from him, whose chain includes 'Abd al-Malik Abu 'Afif, whom Abu Hatim called unknown.
research_evidence: عرزب: براء ثم زاي، وزن أحمد، الكندي. عداده في أهل الشام. ذكره البخاري وابن السكن وغيرهما.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عابس الغفاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4356) lists 'Abis bin 'Abs al-Ghifari, also called 'Abs bin 'Abis, and quotes al-Bukhari that he was a Companion. It notes his reports were transmitted by al-Tabarani and Ibn Shahin, including a report about the plague and six matters he heard from the Prophet.
research_evidence: عابس بن عبس: الغفاريّ. ويقال له عبس بن عابس. قال البخاريّ: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرة بنت الحارث بن بن أبي ضرار ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11496) lists 'Amra bint al-Harith bin Abi Dirar al-Khuza'iyya al-Mustaliqiyya, sister of the Mother of the Believers Juwayriya. It cites a hadith narrated from her by her nephew Muhammad bin 'Amr bin Abi Dirar: 'This world is green and sweet; whoever takes something of it lawfully is blessed in it.'
research_evidence: عمرة بنت الحارث بن أبي ضرار الخزاعية المصطلقية، أخت أم المؤمنين جويرية.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرة بنت يسار ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11522) lists 'Amra bint Yasar bin Uzayhir. It states Abu Musa mentioned her in his supplement (al-Dhayl) on the authority of al-Mustaghfiri, who said she was a Companion.
research_evidence: عمرة بنت يسار بن أزيهر. ذكرها أبو موسى في الذّيل عن المستغفريّ وأنه قال: لها صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عزة بنت خابل ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11476) lists 'Azza bint Khabil al-Khuza'iyya and notes Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) mis-spelled her father's name. It says Ibn Abi 'Asim and al-Tabarani (in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat) transmitted a hadith through Musa bin Ya'qub from 'Ata' bin Mas'ud al-Ka'bi, who narrated from his aunt 'Azza bint Khabil that she came to the Prophet.
research_evidence: عزّة بنت خابل: بالخاء المعجمة والباء الموحدة، الخزاعيّة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: غنام بن ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6931) lists Ghannam bin Aws bin Ghannam bin 'Amr al-Ansari al-Khazraji al-Bayadi. It quotes al-Waqidi and Ibn al-Kalbi that he fought at Badr, and Ibn Hibban, who listed him among the Companions, that he was the father of 'Abdullah bin Ghannam.
research_evidence: غنّام بن أوس بن غنّام بن عمرو بن مالك بن عامر بن بياضة الأنصاري الخزرجي البياضي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: غسان العبدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6927) lists Ghassan al-'Abdi and quotes al-Bukhari that he was a Companion. It quotes Ibn Hibban that his kunya was Abu Yahya, that he was of 'Abd al-Qays, and that he came to the Prophet with a delegation.
research_evidence: غسّان العبديّ قال البخاريّ: له صحبة. وقال ابن حبان: أبو يحيى: من عبد القيس له وفادة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: فضالة بن عبد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 7015, with a cross-reference entry 7006 'Fadala bin 'Abdullah') lists Fadala al-Laythi and quotes al-Baghawi that he is said to be the son of 'Abdullah, or of Wahb bin Bajra. It quotes Abu Nu'aym that he was known as al-Zahrani and was the father of 'Abdullah, while Ibn 'Abd al-Barr treated al-Laythi and al-Zahrani as different people. It cites his hadith on guarding the two afternoon prayers, transmitted by his son 'Abdullah bin Fadala and recorded by Abu Dawud.
research_evidence: فضالة الليثي: قال البغويّ: وقيل هو ابن عبد اللَّه، وقيل بن وهب بن بجرة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: فراس بن عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6983) lists Firas bin 'Amr al-Kinani, then al-Laythi. It quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a Companion, while others said he only saw the Prophet and that his father was the Companion. It relates, via al-Bawardi and Ibn Manda through a chain including a transmitter Ibn Hajar calls a liar, a story that his father brought him to the Prophet for a severe headache and the Prophet passed his fingers over his forehead.
research_evidence: فراس بن عمرو الكناني، ثم الليثي. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة، وقال غيره: له رؤية، ولأبيه صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الفاكه بن عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6969) lists al-Fakih bin 'Amr al-Dari, of the clan of Tamim al-Dari, and quotes Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri that he was a Companion. It adds Ibn Hibban's statement that he was Tamim al-Dari's cousin, who settled at Bayt Jibrin in Palestine and died there.
research_evidence: الفاكه بن عمرو الداريّ: من رهط تميم الداريّ. قال جعفر المستغفري: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الفلتان ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists al-Faltan ibn 'Asim al-Jarmi, maternal uncle of Kulayb, and counts him among the Kufans. It quotes al-Bukhari, citing 'Asim ibn Kulayb, that he was a companion.
research_evidence: الفلتان بفتحتين، ومثناة فوقانية، ابن عاصم الجرمي، خال كليب. يعدّ في الكوفيين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: فاطمة بنت عمرو بن حزم ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba has a short entry for Fatima bint 'Amr ibn Hazm. It says Abu Musa (al-Madini) listed her in his al-Dhayl and quoted al-Mustaghfiri that she was a companion; Abu Musa thought she might be the same as the preceding entry (Fatima bint 'Amr).
research_evidence: فاطمة بنت عمرو بن حزم ذكرها أبو موسى في «الذّيل» ، ونقل عن المستغفريّ أنه قال: لها صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الفريعة بنت وهب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists Furay'a bint Wahb al-Zuhriyya. It reports that the Prophet raised her up with his hand and said: whoever wants to see the maternal aunt of the Messenger of God, let him look at this woman. Ibn Hajar says Abu Musa mentioned her in his al-Dhayl and added nothing more.
research_evidence: فريعة بنت وهب الزهرية ... رفعها النّبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم بيده، وقال: من أراد أن ينظر إلى خالة رسول اللَّه فلينظر إلى هذه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قيس بن سلع ( رضي الله عنه

possible_duplicate_of.core_famous: Umm Qays bint Mihsan bin Khalid

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba says Qays ibn Sal' al-Ansari was listed among the companions by al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Sakan, Ibn Hibban and others. Al-Baghawi says he lived in Medina, and Ibn Hibban says the Prophet prayed for him. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) rejects the variant name Qays ibn Asla'.
research_evidence: قيس بن سلع بفتحتين الأنصاري. ذكره البخاريّ، وابن السّكن، وابن حبّان، وغيرهم في الصحابة، وقال البغوي: سكن المدينة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قيس أبو غنيم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7235, headed Qays ibn Ghunaym) says al-Bukhari and Ibn Hibban list him as a companion counted among the people of Basra, and that his son narrated from him. Ibn Hajar thinks 'ibn' may be a miscopying of 'Abu', and quotes Ibn al-Sakan that he composed verses mourning the Prophet, has no narration from the Prophet, and that his son Ghunaym ibn Qays transmitted those verses.
research_evidence: قيس بن غنيم ... كذا ترجم له البخاري ... وكذا ذكره ابن حبّان، وقال: له صحبة، عداده في أهل البصرة. روى عنه ابنه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قيس بن الحصين بن يزيد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba gives his lineage as Qays ibn al-Husayn ibn Yazid ibn Shaddad ibn Qanan, Dhu al-Ghussa, al-Mazini. Citing Ibn Ishaq, it says he came to the Prophet with a delegation; Ibn Hibban and al-Daraqutni say he was a companion and from Madhhij. The entry goes on to recount the delegation's conversation with the Prophet.
research_evidence: قيس بن الحصين بن يزيد بن شداد بن قنان، ذي الغصّة، المازني. وفد على النبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم، قاله ابن إسحاق
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قيس بن الخشخاش ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7173, headed with the undotted spelling al-Hashas) covers Qays ibn al-Khashkhash, brother of 'Abdullah ibn al-Khashkhash. It says al-Baghawi listed him among the companions and cited al-Bukhari that he narrated from the Prophet, notes the name is spelled with dotted letters (Ibn Shahin used undotted ones), and quotes Ibn Hibban: 'it is said he was a companion'.
research_evidence: ذكره البغويّ في الصحابة ... وقد تقدم حديثه في ترجمة أخيه عبد اللَّه بن الخشخاش، وأنه بمعجمات ... وقال ابن حبّان: يقال (إن) له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قيس بن طخفة ( رضي الله عنه

possible_duplicate_of.core_famous: Umm Qays bint Mihsan bin Khalid

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba says al-Baghawi listed Qays ibn Tikhfa among the companions and said he lived in Medina. Ibn Hibban says he was a companion, that he is also called Qays ibn Tihfa, and that his son Ya'ish narrated from him. Ibn Hajar refers to the dispute over the name discussed under Tikhfa ibn Qays.
research_evidence: قيس بن طخفة ذكره البغويّ في الصحابة، وقال: سكن المدينة. وقال ابن حبّان: له صحبة قال: ويقال قيس بن طهفة، روى عنه ابنه يعيش
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قدامة بن عبد الله البكري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba has a short entry (7101) for Qudama ibn 'Abdullah al-Bakri, quoting Ibn Hibban that he was a companion counted among the people of Kufa. This is a separate entry from the better-known Qudama ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ammar al-Kilabi (7099).
research_evidence: قدامة بن عبد اللَّه البكري. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة، عداده في أهل الكوفة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قتادة بن ربعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba says Ibn Hibban listed Qatada ibn Rib'i among the companions and said he was governor of Mecca. Ibn Hajar worries he may really be Abu Qatada, but notes Abu Qatada never governed Mecca.
research_evidence: قتادة بن ربعي ذكره ابن حبّان في الصحابة في الأسماء في حرف القاف، وقال: له صحبة، وكان عاملا على مكة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قرة بن دعموص ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba traces Qurra ibn Da'mus's lineage to Numayr ibn 'Amir, says he is counted among the Basrans, and says he came to the Prophet together with his paternal uncle. The entry (continued on the next page) cites reports through 'A'idh ibn Rabi'a al-Numayri, who calls Qurra his grandfather, including reports cited by Abu Nu'aym.
research_evidence: قرة بن دعموص بن ربيعة بن عوف بن معاوية بن قريع بن الحارث بن نمير بن عامر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قرة بن هبيرة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba traces Qurra ibn Hubayra's lineage through Qushayr to 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'a (al-'Amiri al-Qushayri). It says al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Manda all counted him a companion, and it cites reports about him through Ibn Abi 'Asim and Ibn Shahin.
research_evidence: قرة بن هبيرة بن عامر بن سلمة بن قشير بن كعب بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صعصعة العامري ثم القشيري
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: قطبة بن قتادة السدوسي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba names him Qutba ibn Qatada ibn Jarir al-Sadusi, Abu al-Huwaysila, and quotes al-Bukhari that he was a companion and Ibn Hibban that he came to the Prophet. The entry discusses his daughter al-Huwaysila and notes that he was the first to conquer al-Ubulla.
research_evidence: قطبة بن قتادة بن جرير السدوسي، أبو الحويصلة. قال البخاريّ: له صحبة. وقال ابن حبان: أتى
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: كعب بن عمرو أبو شريح ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7440) lists Ka'b ibn 'Amr, Abu Shurayh al-Khuza'i, and says Ka'b is one suggested name for him, but Khuwaylid ibn 'Amr is the better-known name.
research_evidence: كعب بن عمرو أبو شريح الخزاعي. قيل: هو اسم خويلد بن عمرو، وخويلد أشهر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: كعب بن عامر السعدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba says Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri called Ka'b ibn 'Amir al-Sa'di a companion, and Ibn Hibban listed him among the companions with the nisba al-Sa'idi. It adds that al-Barudi, via 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', named him among those who fought at Siffin with 'Ali.
research_evidence: كعب بن عامر السعدي له صحبة، قاله جعفر المستغفري. وذكره ابن حبان في الصحابة، فقال الساعدي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: كرز بن علقمة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba traces Kurz ibn 'Alqama's lineage to Salul of Khuza'a. It says he became Muslim on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, lived a long life, went blind late in life, and was one of those who renewed the boundary markers of the Haram in the time of Mu'awiya.
research_evidence: كرز بن علقمة ... الخزاعي ... أسلم يوم الفتح، وعمّر طويلا، وعمي في آخر عمره، وكان ممّن جدّد أنصاب الحرم في زمن معاوية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: كهمس الهلالي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba cites a report, also given by al-Tayalisi and Samawayh, through Mu'awiya ibn Qurra from Kahmas al-Hilali. In it Kahmas says he became Muslim, told the Prophet, then came back a year later worn thin from constant fasting, and the Prophet told him not to torment himself but to fast the month of patience (Ramadan) and one day each month.
research_evidence: من طريق معاوية بن قرة، عن كهمس الهلالي، قال: أسلمت فأتيت النبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم فأخبرته بإسلامي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: كريمة بنت كلثوم ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba has a short entry for Karima bint Kulthum al-Himyariyya. It says she was already mentioned in the biography of 'Akkaf ibn Wada'a, and that some say she is Zaynab bint Kulthum.
research_evidence: كريمة بنت كلثوم الحميرية تقدم ذكرها في ترجمة عكاف بن وداعة. وقيل هي زينب بنت كلثوم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: لبيد بن ربيعة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba names him Labid ibn Rabi'a ibn 'Amir ... al-Kilabi al-Ja'fari, Abu 'Aqil, the famous poet. The entry describes him as a pre-Islamic poet who later became Muslim and recounts his reply when the caliph 'Umar asked about his poetry after Islam. The editor's note cites Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isti'ab, al-Waqidi's al-Maghazi and Ibn Hisham's Sira among its references.
research_evidence: لبيد بن ربيعة بن عامر بن مالك بن جعفر بن كلاب بن ربيعة بن صعصعة الكلابي الجعفري، أبو عقيل الشاعر المشهور
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: لبي بن ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba explains the spelling (Lubayy ibn Laba) and quotes al-Bukhari that he was a companion, with Abu Balj al-Saghir narrating from him. Abu Hatim al-Razi says he lived in Wasit, and he and Ibn Hibban say 'it is said he was a companion'. Ibn al-Sakan says no hearing from the Prophet was found for him.
research_evidence: لبيّ بن لبا ... قال البخاريّ: له صحبة. روى عنه أبو بلج الصغير وقال أبو حاتم الرّازيّ: كان يكون بواسط
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مالك بن عبد الله الأوسي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7660) says Malik ibn 'Abdullah al-Awsi narrated the hadith 'if a slave-woman commits zina', and refers the reader to the discussion under 'Abdullah ibn Malik and Shibl ibn Khulayd.
research_evidence: مالك بن عبد الله الأوسي روى حديث: إذا زنت الأمة وقد تقدم الكلام عليه في عبد اللَّه بن مالك وفي شبل بن خليد
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مالك بن عبادة أبو موسى الغافقي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7657) says Malik ibn 'Ubada, also called Ibn 'Abdullah, is Abu Musa al-Ghafiqi, best known by his kunya. His full entry is in the kunya section, and he is also mentioned under Malik ibn 'Abdullah al-Ma'afiri.
research_evidence: مالك بن عبادة وقيل ابن عبد اللَّه، أبو موسى الغافقي، مشهور بكنيته. يأتي في الكنى
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مالك بن عبد الله الخزاعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7661) says Malik ibn 'Abdullah al-Khuza'i, also called al-Khath'ami, lived in Kufa according to al-Baghawi, and al-Bukhari counted him a companion. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Abi 'Asim and al-Baghawi report through his nephew Sulayman ibn Bishr al-Khuza'i that he campaigned with the Prophet and never prayed behind an imam whose obligatory prayer was lighter than the Prophet's.
research_students: Sulayman ibn Bishr al-Khuza'i (his sister's son)
research_evidence: مالك بن عبد الله الخزاعي ويقال الخثعميّ. قال البغويّ: خزاعيّ سكن الكوفة وقال البخاري: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مالك بن عبد الله الخثعمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7663) gives Malik ibn 'Abdullah ibn Sinan al-Khath'ami's lineage and says he was known as 'Malik of the raiding parties' (Malik al-Saraya). The entry continues that he led the summer campaigns under Mu'awiya, then Yazid, then 'Abd al-Malik, and notes a hadith that Malik heard from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.
research_evidence: مالك بن عبد الله بن سنان بن سرح بن وهب بن الأقيصر بن قحافة ... الخثعميّ. كان يعرف بمالك السّرايا
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مالك بن الخشخاش ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba has a cross-reference entry (7635) for Malik ibn al-Khashkhash al-'Anbari, saying he was already covered under 'Ubayd ibn al-Khashkhash. An earlier cross-reference (7629) notes the name is spelled with dotted letters.
research_evidence: مالك بن الخشخاس العنبري تقدم في عبيد بن الحسحاس
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مسلم بن عمرو بن أبي عقرب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7996) names him Muslim ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Aqrab Khuwaylid ibn Khalid and quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a companion. Al-Baghawi calls him Muslim ibn 'Amr Abu 'Aqrab, father of Abu Nawfal ibn Abi 'Aqrab. The entry goes on to discuss other forms of his name and cross-references al-Bukhari's Tarikh.
research_evidence: مسلم بن عمرو بن أبي عقرب خويلد بن خالد. له صحبة، هكذا قال: ابن حبّان، وقال البغويّ: مسلم بن عمرو أبو عقرب
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مسلم والد رائطة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7999) says Muslim, father of Rayta (Ra'ita), was present with the Prophet at Hunayn; his original name was Ghurab and the Prophet renamed him Muslim. His daughter narrated this from him, and al-Bukhari included it in al-Adab al-Mufrad and al-Tarikh al-Kabir. Al-Baghawi says he lived in Mecca.
research_evidence: مسلم غير منسوب، والد ريطة. روت عنه بنته أنه قال: شهدت مع النبي صلى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم حنينا
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مسلم والد عوسجة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8002) quotes Ibn Hibban that Muslim, father of 'Awsaja, was a companion; al-Baghawi says he thinks he lived in Kufa. Al-Baghawi's chain runs through his son 'Awsaja, who reports his father saying he travelled with the Prophet and saw him wipe over his leather socks.
research_evidence: مسلم والد عوسجة. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة. وقال البغوي: أحسبه كان بالكوفة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ميمون بن سنباذ ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8303) names him Maymun ibn Sunbadh al-'Uqayli, kunya Abu al-Mughira, says he was originally from Yemen, that his hadith is counted among the Basrans, and that he was a companion. The entry (continued on the next page) quotes a report of a man who met him after leaving al-Hasan's gathering and was told he was a companion of the Prophet.
research_evidence: ميمون بن سنباذ العقيليّ، يكنى أبا المغيرة ... أصله من اليمن، وحديثه في البصريّين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مدرك بن عوف ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7871) names him Mudrik ibn 'Awf al-Bajali al-Ahmasi. Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri counted him a companion; Ibn Hibban listed him among the companions and then again among the Successors. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) says his companionship is disputed, that Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated from him, and that he heard from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.
research_evidence: مدرك بن عوف البجلي الأحمسي. ذكره جعفر المستغفري، وقال: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مدلوك ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7877) lists Mudluk al-Fazari, a client (mawla) of Fazara, with the kunya Abu Sufyan. It quotes Ibn Abi Hatim that he was a companion, and notes Muhammad ibn Sa'd listed him among the companions who settled in al-Sham.
research_evidence: مدلوك الفزاري: مولاهم، أبو سفيان. قال ابن أبي حاتم: له صحبة. وذكره محمد بن سعد فيمن نزل الشام من الصحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ميسرة الفجر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8301) says al-Bukhari, al-Baghawi, Ibn al-Sakan and others listed Maysara al-Fajr among the companions. It cites his report, via Budayl ibn Maysara from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, that he asked the Prophet 'When were you a prophet?' and was told 'while Adam was between the spirit and the body'.
research_evidence: وأخرجوا من طريق بديل بن ميسرة، عن عبد اللَّه بن شقيق، عن ميسرة الفجر، قال: قلت
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مروان بن قيس السلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7932) names Marwan ibn Qays al-Asadi, also called al-Sulami. It quotes al-Bukhari that he was a companion and that his son narrated from him, and notes that al-Baghawi and al-Tabarani transmitted his report through Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi.
research_evidence: مروان بن قيس: الأسديّ . ويقال: السلميّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: معبد بن مسعود ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8123) names Ma'bad ibn Mas'ud al-Sulami, brother of Mujalid and Mujashi'. It quotes al-Bukhari, al-Bazzar and Ibn Hibban that he was a companion, and cites a report via Asim al-Ahwal from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi that Mujashi' brought his brother Ma'bad to the Prophet after the Conquest to pledge allegiance.
research_evidence: معبد بن مسعود السلمي أخو مجالد، ومجاشع. قال البخاريّ، والبزّار، وابن حبّان: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مرزوق الصيقل ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7916) says al-Askari and others counted Marzuq al-Sayqal as a companion, and Ibn Hibban said it is reported that he was one; Ibn Abd al-Barr noted weakness in his hadith's chain. It cites a report via Abu al-Hakam that he polished the Prophet's sword Dhu al-Fiqar, transmitted by al-Baghawi and al-Tabarani. Ibn Hajar notes the report alone does not prove companionship.
research_evidence: مرزوق الصيقل قال العسكريّ وغيره: له صحبة. وقال ابن حبّان: يقال إن له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مكرز ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8211) gives Mikraz ibn Hafs ibn al-Akhyaf of Quraysh (Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy) and says Ibn Hibban counted him among the companions, though this is debated. It notes he came to ransom Suhayl ibn Amr after Badr, as recorded by Ibn Ishaq and al-Waqidi. Al-Marzubani lists him in his dictionary of poets as pre-Islamic, which leaves his conversion uncertain.
research_evidence: مكرز بن حفص بن الأخيف، بالخاء المعجمة والياء المثناة، ابن علقمة بن عبد الحارث بن منقذ بن عمرو بن بغيض بن عامر بن لؤيّ القرشي العامريّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مسعود بن هنيدة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7978) quotes Ibn Hibban that Mas'ud ibn Hunayda al-Aslami was a companion, and identifies him as a client (mawla) of Abu Tamim Aws ibn Hajar (also given as Tamim ibn Hajar). It says he served as a guide for the Prophet on a journey and was present at the campaign of al-Muraysi', citing al-Waqidi, Ibn Sa'd, al-Baghawi, Ibn Manda and al-Tabarani.
research_evidence: يقال اسم أبيه هنيدة. قال ابن حبّان: مسعود بن هنيدة الأسلميّ له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مرداس بن عروة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7900) lists Mirdas ibn Urwa al-Amiri, whom al-Baghawi and Ibn Hibban call al-Thaqafi. Ibn al-Sakan counted him among the companions and among the people of Kufa, and Ibn Hibban said he was a companion. His hadith was transmitted by al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Sakan and al-Bayhaqi via al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa.
research_evidence: مرداس بن عروة العامريّ ذكره ابن السّكن في الصحابة، وقال: معدود في الكوفيين، ونسبه البغويّ وابن حبّان
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مرة بن كعب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7924) lists Murra ibn Ka'b al-Bahzi and says he is said to be the same as Ka'b ibn Murra, entered under the letter kaf. It cites a report via Ayyub from Abu Qilaba from Abu al-Ash'ath about speakers in Syria during the strife around Uthman, and notes several variant versions of it.
research_evidence: مرة بن كعب البهزي يقال: هو كعب بن مرّة الماضي في الكاف. روى أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن أبي الأشعث
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: المطلب بن حنطب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8044) gives al-Muttalib ibn Hantab ibn al-Harith ibn Ubayd Allah of Banu Makhzum, father of Abdullah ibn Hantab. It cites Ibn Ishaq that he was taken captive at Badr and later became Muslim, and mentions a report attributed to him whose chain has discrepancies.
research_evidence: المطلب بن حنطب بن الحارث بن عبيد اللَّه بن مخزوم، أبو عبد اللَّه بن حنطب
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مجدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7744) lists Majdhi (also spelled Majdi) al-Damri, mentioned by Ibn al-Sakan and others; Ibn Hibban said it is reported that he was a companion. Ibn Abd al-Barr gives his hadith as coming through his descendants (his son's line via Ata), and Ibn Hajar corrects two names in that chain citing al-Bukhari's Tarikh and Ibn Abi Asim.
research_evidence: مجذي الضمري ذكره ابن السّكن وغيره، وقال ابن حبّان: يقال إن له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: منيب الأزدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 5131) lists Munib al-Azdi with the kunya Abu Mudrik (not Abu Malik), and says his hadith was transmitted by his grandson Munib ibn Mudrik ibn Munib, from his father, from his grandfather. Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8268) gives him as Munib Abu Ayyub al-Azdi al-Ghamidi, a companion per al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim, counted among the people of al-Sham.
research_evidence: منيب الأَزْدِيّ أَبُو مدرك روى حديثه منيب بْن مدرك بْن منيب، عن أبيه، عن جده
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مشمرج ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8018) gives Mushamrij ibn Khalid al-Sa'di, grandfather of the hadith scholar Ali ibn Hujr ibn Iyas ibn Muqatil ibn Mushamrij, and quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a companion. It cites a report via Ibn al-Sakan that he came to the Prophet with the delegation of Abd al-Qays and was given a garment and a written grant of water rights.
research_evidence: مشمرج بضم أوله وفتح الشين المعجمة وسكون الميم وكسر الراء بعدها جيم، ابن خالد السعدي، جد علي بن حجر المحدث
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مزيدة العصري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7937) discusses Mazida al-Asri of Abd al-Qays, whose father Ibn Manda names Jabir and Ibn al-Kalbi names Malik. It says Mazida, the maternal grandfather of Hud ibn Abdullah al-Asri, has a hadith in al-Tirmidhi and others, and quotes al-Baghawi that al-Bukhari said 'Mazida al-Asri was a companion'. Ibn Hajar separates him from a later Mazida who was a Kharijite judge under Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a.
research_evidence: مزيدة: بن جابر العبديّ العصري. كذا سمى ابن مندة أباه، وسماه ابن الكلبيّ مالكا
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: مازن بن الغضوبة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7601) gives Mazin ibn al-Ghadubah ibn Irab of the Nabhan branch of Tayy. Citing Ibn al-Sakan, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Fakihi, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Qani', it tells how he broke his idol, came to the Prophet and accepted Islam, and how the Prophet prayed for him.
research_evidence: مازن بن الغضوبة بن عراب بن بشر بن خطامة بن سعد بن ثعلبة بن نصر بن سعد بن أسود بن نبهان
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: النعمان بن رازية ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8759) describes al-Nu'man ibn Raziya al-Azdi al-Lahabi as chief (arif) and standard-bearer of the Azd. It says al-Bukhari, Ibn Manda, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Hibban counted him as a companion, and that he lived in Homs.
research_evidence: النّعمان بن رازية براء ثم زاي مكسورة بعدها تحتانية، والأزديّ، ثم اللهبيّ، عريف الأزد، وصاحب رايتهم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نعيم بن أوس الرهاوي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8792) has a brief entry for Nu'aym ibn Aws al-Rahawi, saying only that he is reported to have been a companion. No narrators or further details are given.
research_evidence: نعيم بن أوس الرّهاوي : يقال إن له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نفير بن مجيب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8815) lists Nufayr ibn Mujib al-Thumali and quotes Ibn Hibban that he is reported to have been a companion. It adds that his name is also given as Sufyan, under which he has an entry in the letter sin.
research_evidence: نفير بن مجيب الثّمالي قال ابن حبّان: يقال: إن له صحبة، ويقال اسمه سفيان. تقدم في السّين.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نمير بن خرشة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8829) lists Numayr ibn Kharasha ibn Rabi'a of the tribe of Thaqif among the companions and gives his lineage back to Thaqif, citing Ibn Hibban. No further details are given.
research_evidence: نمير بن خرشة بن ربيعة بن الحارث بن حبيب بن الحارث بن حطيط بن جشم بن ثقيف الثقفيّ. نسبه ابن حبّان.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نضلة بن عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8738) gives Nadla ibn Amr ibn Ahban of Ghifar and quotes Ibn al-Sakan that he was a companion. It says Ahmad, al-Baghawi, Thabit in al-Dala'il and Ibn Qani' transmitted his report through his descendant Muhammad ibn Ma'n ibn Nadla ibn Amr, and links it to a hadith cited under Makram al-Ghifari.
research_evidence: نضلة بن عمرو بن أهبان بن حلّان بن جعاف بن حبيب بن غفار الغفاريّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نهيك بن صريم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8841) quotes Ibn Hibban that Nahik ibn Suraym al-Sakuni was a companion; Abu Zur'a al-Dimashqi listed him among the companions who settled in al-Sham, and Abd al-Samad among those of Homs. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Manda transmitted his hadith, through Abu Idris al-Khawlani, about fighting the polytheists by the Jordan River.
research_evidence: نهيك بن صريم السكوني قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة، وذكره أبو زرعة الدمشقيّ فيمن نزل الشّام من الصّحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نعمي ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11819) lists Nu'ma bint Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and quotes Ibn Manda that she is mentioned but has no narrations. Ibn Hajar adds that al-Tabarani transmitted a report via Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata in which the Prophet asked about Ja'far's children looking thin.
research_evidence: نعمى بنت جعفر بن أبي طالب. قال ابن مندة: لها ذكر، وليست لها رواية.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نويلة بنت أسلم ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11830) lists Nuwayla bint Aslam (or bint Muslim) al-Ansariyya al-Harithiyya, noting that transmitters give her father's name differently. The editor's notes point to her entries in al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Istibsar and Tajrid Asma' al-Sahaba.
research_evidence: نويلة بنت أسلم: أو مسلم، الأنصاريّة الحارثيّة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: نسيكة ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11816) lists Nusayka, mother of Amr ibn al-Jallas. Habiba bint Sim'an narrated from her and al-Tabarani recorded her hadith, in which she describes seeing the Prophet at A'isha's house and a meal of barley bread and meat.
research_evidence: نسيكة والدة عمرو بن الجلاس روت عنها حبيبة بنت سمعان، أخرج حديثها الطّبرانيّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: وهب بن قيس بن أبان الثقفي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9193) lists Wahb ibn Qays ibn Aban al-Thaqafi among the companions. The entry only notes that he was already mentioned in the entry on his brother Sufyan ibn Qays.
research_evidence: ٩١٩٣- وهب بن قيس بن أبان الثقفيّ.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: وهب بن محصن ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9188) lists Wahb ibn Abdullah ibn Mihsan al-Asadi, better known by his kunya Abu Sinan, and quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a companion. It notes his name is also given as Abdullah ibn Wahb or as Wahb ibn Mihsan, and that Muslim preferred Abdullah ibn Wahb. A separate short entry (9196) says Wahb ibn Mihsan al-Asadi is this same man, named by some after his grandfather.
research_evidence: وهب بن عبد الله بن محصن الأسديّ، أبو سنان، مشهور بكنيته. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة، ويأتي في الكنى. ويقال اسمه عبد اللَّه بن وهب، ويقال: هو وهب بن محصن
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: وبر بن مشهر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9123) quotes al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Hibban that Wabr ibn Mushahhir al-Hanafi was a companion. Ibn Abi Asim, Ibn al-Sakan and al-Tabarani transmitted his report via Hajib ibn Qudama from Isa ibn Khuthaym, about rejecting envoys who testified to Musaylima's prophethood.
research_evidence: وبر بن مشهّر الحنفيّ. قال البخاريّ، وابن السّكن، وابن حبّان: له صحبة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: وبر بن يحنس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9124) quotes Ibn Hibban that Wabr ibn Yuhannis al-Kalbi is reported to have been a companion. It cites al-Waqidi that in the year 10 AH he came to the Abna' from the Prophet, and mentions that several people became Muslim through him.
research_evidence: وبر بن يحنّس الكلبيّ. قال ابن حبّان: يقال له صحبة. وقال الواقديّ: وفي سنة عشر قدم وبر بن يحنّس
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هبيب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8956) gives Hubayb ibn Mughaffal of Ghifar, a companion who took part in the conquest of Egypt. It says he has a hadith with a sound chain in Ahmad's Musnad about the lower garment (izar). After the killing of Uthman he withdrew to a valley between Maryut and the Fayyum, which became known as Wadi Hubayb.
research_evidence: هبيب بموحدتين مصغرا، ابن مغفل، بضم أوله وسكون الغين المعجمة وكسر الفاء
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Hlal bin Umayya bin 'Amir bin Qays bin 'Abdul A'lam bin 'Amir bin K'ab al-Wafaqi al-Ansari
full_name_ar: هلال بن أمية ( رضي الله عنه

possible_duplicate_of.core_famous: Sukhta bint Qays bin Abi Ka'b

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8998) gives Hilal ibn Umayya ibn Amir of Banu Waqif of the Ansar, and says he fought at Badr and later battles. He was one of the three whose repentance was accepted after they stayed behind from Tabuk, and he is linked to the li'an (mutual cursing) episode. Ibn Hajar also discusses chains suggesting he lived into the Umayyad period.
research_evidence: هلال بن أمية بن عامر بن قيس بن عبد الأعلم بن عامر بن كعب بن واقف الأنصاريّ الواقفيّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هلال بن الحارث أبو الحمراء ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9001) lists Hilal ibn al-Harith as Abu al-Hamra', a freedman (mawla) of the Prophet, well known by his kunya, and refers the reader to his full entry in the kunya section.
research_evidence: هلال بن الحارث: أبو الحمراء- مولى النّبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم، مشهور بكنيته. ويأتي في الكنى.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هند بن أسماء ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9024) says his lineage was given under his father Asma' (ibn Haritha). It quotes al-Bukhari and Ibn al-Sakan that he was a companion, and Ibn al-Sakan that he died during the caliphate of Mu'awiya; Ahmad transmitted a report about him via Ibn Ishaq.
research_evidence: هند بن أسماء: تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أبيه أسماء، قال البخاريّ: له صحبة، وقال ابن السّكن: له صحبة، ومات في خلافة معاوية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هزال الأسلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8974) gives him as Hazzal ibn Yazid ibn Dhi'ab al-Aslami and quotes Ibn Hibban that he was a companion. His hadith, in al-Nasa'i, comes through his son Nu'aym ibn Hazzal: Hazzal had a slave girl with whom Ma'iz had relations, and Hazzal told Ma'iz to go and confess to the Prophet.
research_evidence: هزّال بن يزيد بن ذئاب بن كليب بن عامر بن جذيمة بن مازن الأسلميّ. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هلال الأسلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9008) says Hilal al-Aslami has a hadith on sacrificial animals transmitted by Ahmad and Ibn Majah with a good (hasan) chain. Ibn Hibban counted him a companion; Ibn Mandah called him Hilal ibn Abi Hilal and Ibn Qani' called him Hilal ibn Muslim.
research_evidence: هلال الأسلميّ. له حديث في الأضاحي، أخرجه أحمد وابن ماجة بسند حسن
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: هداج ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8961) lists Huddaj al-Hanafi, counted among the people of Medina, who lived in the pre-Islamic era. Al-Baghawi, Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Mandah narrate via Abu 'Ammar Hashim ibn Ghatafan from his son 'Abdullah ibn Huddaj a report about a man who came to the Prophet with his beard dyed yellow.
research_evidence: هدّاج الحنفي يعدّ في المدنيين ... عن عبد اللَّه بن هداج، عن أبيه، وكان هداج أدرك الجاهلية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يعلى بن سيابة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9381) states that Ya'la ibn Siyaba is Ya'la ibn Murra al-Thaqafi, while noting that scholars such as Abu Hatim and Ibn Qani' treated them as two separate people. The following entry on Ya'la ibn Murra says he took part in Khaybar and the conquest of Mecca and narrated from the Prophet and from 'Ali.
research_evidence: يعلى بن سيابة وهو ابن مرة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يزيد بن مالك بن عبد الله أبو سبرة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9326) lists Yazid ibn Malik ibn 'Abdullah al-Ju'fi, quoting Ibn Hibban that he was a companion, and notes others identify him as Abu Sabra, treated in the kunya section.
research_evidence: يزيد بن مالك بن عبد اللَّه الجعفيّ ... له صحبة. وقال غيره: هو أبو سبرة الآتي في الكنى
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يزيد بن أسد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9249) calls him Yazid ibn Asad ibn Kurz al-Bajali, grandfather of the governor Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Qasri. Ibn Sa'd placed him in the fourth tier of companions as one who came to the Prophet in a delegation; al-Bukhari said he heard the Prophet, and Abu Hatim and Ibn Hibban counted him a companion. His hadith in the Musnad of 'Abd ibn Humayd: 'O Yazid ibn Asad, love for people what you love for yourself', graded sahih by al-Hakim.
research_students: Asad (his son, father of Khalid al-Qasri)
research_evidence: يزيد بن أسد بن كرز، بضم الكاف وسكون الراء بعدها زاي، البجليّ. جدّ خالد بن عبد اللَّه القسريّ الأمير
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: يزيد بن سيف ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 9292) gives him as Yazid ibn Sayf ibn Haritha al-Tamimi al-Yarbu'i, a companion per Abu Hatim and Ibn Hibban. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) says his hadith on the 'arif (tribal overseer) is held by his descendants; al-Baghawi, Ibn al-Sakan, al-Tabarani and Ibn Qani' narrate it via Mawdud ibn al-Harith: the Prophet warned that the 'arif will be pushed into the Fire.
research_evidence: يزيد بن سيف بن حارثة التميمي اليربوعي. قال ابن أبي حاتم، عن أبيه: له صحبة، وكذا قال ابن حبان
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)
